annotation.title_clean: Draft articles on autonomous weapon systems – prohibitions and other regulatory measures on the basis of international humanitarian law
annotation.title_en: Draft articles on autonomous weapon systems – prohibitions and other regulatory measures on the basis of international humanitarian law
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Australia, Canada, Czechia, Estonia, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Republic of Korea, United Kingdom and others (CCW GGE working paper)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2025/WP.7)
annotation.summary_en: Working paper submitted by a group of states to the CCW GGE on LAWS, proposing seven draft articles that clarify how IHL (distinction, proportionality, precautions, accountability) applies to autonomous weapon systems. It annexes the Guiding Principles and consensus conclusions. The articles create no new legal obligations.
key_provisions_or_claims: Autonomous weapon systems must not be designed to target civilians, cause excessive incidental harm, or act outside commander responsibility
Development requires rigorous testing, legal reviews and design precautions, including limits on targets, duration and area, and reduced automation bias
Commanders must apply distinction, proportionality and precautions when using such systems
States must deploy them within a responsible chain of command with training, human-machine interfaces and incident investigation
Draft articles clarify existing IHL and neither create nor derogate from legal obligations
